_meta.indication: WAINUA is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter study of eplontersen (45 mg every 4 weeks) using inotersen as an active control, with efficacy assessed against an external placebo group from another study (NCT01737398).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects with stage 1 or stage 2 hATTR-PN with documented genetic mutation in the TTR gene and NIS of 10 to 130 at baseline.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The efficacy endpoints were change from baseline to Week 35 in the modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) composite score and change from baseline to Week 35 in the Norfolk Quality of Life-Diabetic Neuropathy (QoL-DN) total score; change from baseline in serum TTR concentration was also assessed.
pivotal_trials.n: 144 subjects randomized to eplontersen, 24 to concurrent inotersen, and 60 in the external placebo group.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 35, mNIS+7 change from baseline was 0.2 (WAINUA) vs 9.2 (placebo), treatment difference LS Mean -9.0 (95% CI -13.5, -4.5), p<0.001; Norfolk QoL-DN change was -3.1 vs 8.7, treatment difference -11.8 (95% CI -16.8, -6.8), p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥9% of patients) were vitamin A decreased (15%) and vomiting (9%); other reactions reported in at least 5% of patients included proteinuria (8%), injection site reactions (7%), and blurred vision (6%). Three serious adverse reactions of atrioventricular (AV) heart block (2%) occurred, including 1 case of complete AV block.
target_moa: Eplontersen is a transthyretin-directed antisense oligonucleotide-GalNAc conjugate that causes hepatic-targeted degradation of mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA through direct binding, reducing serum TTR protein and TTR deposits in tissues.

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; FDA concurred that eplontersen would not require a Boxed Warning for thrombocytopenia or glomerulonephritis given the absence of empirical evidence suggesting increased risk.

rems.type: No REMS required; FDA concurred that eplontersen would not require a REMS program for thrombocytopenia or glomerulonephritis.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues in the intended population.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA (not priority) approved on the basis of a single adequate and well-controlled study (ION-682884-CS3) with confirmatory pharmacodynamic/mechanistic TTR-reduction data; eplontersen held orphan drug designation for the polyneuropathy of hATTR amyloidosis and was not an accelerated approval.

requirement.text: 4564-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to eplontersen during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
